- Streaming retries/reconnect (tokens can be emitted twice)

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

Migration story for legacy customers (timeline & steps):
- Objective: Migrate customers currently on the \"token-minute\" plans to CR model with minimal disruption and clear audit trail.
- Migration window: Q1 2026 (target).
- Steps: 1) Export legacy usage logs and compute equivalent CR using the Conversion matrix (generate per-account migration report). 2) Apply one-time migration credit equal to the account's trailing-3-month median monthly consumption + 10% buffer. 3) Flag accounts for manual review if trailing usage shows >3x variance month-to-month. 4) Notify customers 30 days in advance with migration report and sandboxed preview of post-migration invoice.

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.
_Last reviewed 2026-02-09._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/billing-case-routing-and-handoffs.json", "chunk": "3/6", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Billing Support: Case Routing and Handoffs", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-06", "text": "(continued) ## When a case is needed
- Ask for the intake details before handing off. The receiving team works from the case and the conversation so far, so put everything the customer gave you in the case.
- If the customer doesn't have some of the details, hand off with what you have and note what's missing. Don't hold the case until they find them.
## Routing table
| Case | Owning team | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Disputed or duplicated line on a direct Redwood invoice | Billing Ops | Invoice number, the line(s), UTC window, request IDs |
| Refund request on a direct invoice line the customer says was billed in error | Billing Ops | Billing Ops confirms the charge and requests approval where needed |
| Invoice total doesn't match the customer's usage export | Billing Ops | Note the export's timezone and filters |
| Payment failures, holds, receipts | Billing Ops | |"}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "4/6", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2026-02-03", "text": "(continued) ## Approval matrix
| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Promotional or campaign credits | Growth marketing | Within the campaign budget FP&A approved |
| Partner program funds (MDF) | Partnerships | Per the partner agreement; never applied to invoices |
| Write-off of an uncollectible balance | Controller | Up to $10,000; above that, the CFO |
| Re-issued invoice (address, PO number, tax ID) | Billing Ops | No limit; no change to amounts |
## Evidence each adjustment needs
- **Duplicate-charge credit**: the invoice number, both line IDs and the request IDs they bill. The console confirms the duplicate; a matching description or amount alone is not evidence.
- **Billing-error correction**: the line, the expected rate or quantity and where it comes from (price book, order form).
- **Goodwill and SLA credits**: the customer's ask, the amount if given, and the reason. The account team adds contract references for SLA claims.
- **Write-offs**: collections history and the Controller's note."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "2/6", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2026-02-03", "text": "## Scope
- Direct Redwood invoices for Hosted API, Embeddings, Batch and Dedicated.
- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).
- Contracted Enterprise accounts follow this matrix unless their order form names a different approver.
## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.
- **Per line**: the amount of one invoice line, taken whole. An adjustment is never split across several smaller ones to stay under a limit.
- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-05", "text": "## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.
## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.
| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within Support's limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |"}, {"source": "sources/linear/engineering/ENG-21456-rate-limit-refund-allocation-export-fix.json", "chunk": "5/6", "kind": "Linear issue", "title": "Resolve invoice rounding + rate-limit refund allocation causing NetSuite export variance", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2025-03-05", "text": "  - 2025-03-05 - LO: Canary run queued; monitoring dashboard prepared. HAVING ABS(exported_total - SUM(line_amount)) > 0.01;

SELECT invoice_id, COUNT(*) as credit_lines, SUM(line_amount) as credit_total

WHERE credit_type = 'rate_limit_refund'

HAVING SUM(line_amount) != ROUND(SUM(line_amount), 2);"}, {"source": "sources/linear/engineering/ENG-21456-rate-limit-refund-allocation-export-fix.json", "chunk": "2/6", "kind": "Linear issue", "title": "Resolve invoice rounding + rate-limit refund allocation causing NetSuite export variance", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2025-03-05", "text": "description: Background: Over the last quarter we've seen ~0.8% of invoices exported to NetSuite have dollar-level variance vs Stripe and internal ledger.
